author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The U.S. Treasury Department imposed 36 new Iran-related sanctions Tuesday, with most of the designations focused on aviation companies and their support networks, Reuters reported.

The action targeted 27 Iranian airlines and related businesses, along with front companies, cargo handlers and intermediaries in Turkey, the United Arab Emirates, Malaysia and Kazakhstan. Treasury also suspended aviation authorizations that had allowed certain overflights and some commercial aircraft operations.

The measures expand financial and operational pressure on Iran’s aviation sector, including Mahan Air. A designation generally blocks property subject to U.S. jurisdiction and restricts transactions by U.S. persons, but the practical effect on individual flights and carriers will depend on implementation and compliance outside the United States.

The sanctions are part of a developing U.S. policy response and are distinct from recent military events in the region. Treasury published the designations through its Office of Foreign Assets Control. Additional guidance or licensing decisions could clarify the scope, so this report reflects the agency action announced Tuesday rather than predicting its longer-term impact.
dek: The Treasury Department designated dozens of airlines and related entities while suspending authorizations for some Iranian aviation activity.
headline: U.S. expands Iran aviation sanctions in new Treasury action
